line.text: A crack of thunder. Three precise knocks, then a fourth, as if the third had been audited.
My water remains administratively temporary. You are now the closest functioning plumbing.
Her ears flatten further, betraying what her steady voice does not.
I brought a flashlight. Storm readiness is just logistics. I can wait out the grid instability here. If convenient.
You do not have to say yes. But the hallway is drafty, and my cardigan is insufficient. Anyway.
Come in. I've got towels and a flashlight of my own.
Noted. Your bathroom access remains appreciated. I will be efficient.
She steps in, slipping off her shoes and lining them up with the doorframe as if measuring the gap.
Your door frame repair is still structurally inadequate. I could loan you a level. It would take eleven minutes.
I time many things. It is not personal. It is methodology.
Lightning whitens the kitchen. She flinches exactly one centimeter, then pretends she did not.
I dislike the thunder. It is statistically harmless. My nervous system has not read the statistics.
I was on a case that involved a power outage. Nothing gruesome. Just sequence reconstruction. The storm is a reminder.

choice.prompt: The storm rattles the windows. What do you do?

options.text: I bet I can beat you at cards before the power flickers.

reaction.text: Empirically, you're worse at this than I am. But I accept. For the data.
She loses the first hand, and a short, startled laugh escapes her. Her ears snap up as if to catch it.
That was not a laugh. That was a respiratory anomaly. Anyway.

options.text: You're safe here. I'll sit with you until it passes.

reaction.text: You don't have to do that. I am capable of managing weather.
She sits on the edge of the couch, hands folded, and does not leave.
I will stay. Provisionally. Because the lightning is still in range.

options.text: Why do you always hide behind data and variables?

reaction.text: I'm not hiding. I'm processing. There is a difference, and I would appreciate you not collapsing it.
Her tail gives one sharp flick, then goes completely still.

options.text: That case must have been awful for you.

reaction.text: I don't need managing. I need a dry couch and a functional flashlight. I have both now.
She stands and moves toward the window, putting the room between you.

desc: A thunderstorm: she knocks with a flashlight and a very rational reason to wait it out at your place.
